prerequisites: High proficiency in Electrotechnics is mandatory
Good understanding of steady-state and transient analysis techniques of single-phase and three-phase circuits

learning_outcomes.text: Multidisciplinary knowledge of the regulatory, methodological, technological, and instrumental context related to the energy transition of systems, services, and products.
Systems knowledge of the methodologies, technologies, and applied aspects of electrical engineering.
Knowledge of electronic components and systems and their application in the automation, production, management, and distribution sectors of electrical engineering.
Knowledge of advanced analysis and design tools (mechanical, electrical, or multi-physics) for the modeling and numerical simulation of components and systems.
To Apply engineering knowledge to develop models of complex systems.
To Apply acquired theoretical knowledge to the development and application of innovative systems in the fields of robotics, automation, and electrical engineering.
To Propose, develop, and apply alternative and innovative methodologies for the development of products and services in the context of the ecological transition.
Problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently.
To Communicate, to work in a team, and to make independent decisions.
To Conduct literature research and use databases and other information sources.
To Design and to manage experimental studies, to collect and to interpret data and its uncertainties, and to draw conclusions.
To be able to process complex information and data from multiple sources and to analyze and to manage multidisciplinary topics.
To be able to work in an interdisciplinary context understanding the results of the work of others.
To be able to communicate the results of one's work and activities unambiguously at a level that facilitates teamwork and collaboration.
Ability to effectively and creatively address the changing issues associated with innovation in robotics, automation, and electrical engineering technologies.
Ability to develop logical reasoning that, based on specific hypotheses, leads to the subsequent demonstration of a thesis.
Ability to undertake independent in-depth research that requires bibliographic analysis and the study of current knowledge.
Ability to apply engineering knowledge to develop models of complex systems.
Ability to carry out engineering projects while working in a multidisciplinary environment.
Advanced ability to conduct complex experiments and to manage instrumentation and advanced software.

Ability to analyze and model mechanical/electrical/propulsion components and systems: problems and models underlying industrial engineering, with particular reference to mechanical and energy engineering.
Advanced ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, procedures and methods, including the use of theoretical models, with awareness of their limitations and potential.
Ability to critically evaluate data and results and draw appropriate conclusions, being aware of the level of uncertainty that may affect them.
Ability to achieve preparation adequate for access to third-cycle studies (attendance at second-level masters and doctoral schools) to further deepen knowledge and skills in research.
Ability to analyze technologies of plants, components and processes and engineering methods and their economic implications.
Ability to identify, formulate and solve industrial engineering problems, defining specifications and technical, social, environmental and commercial constraints.
Ability to analyze, design and manage integrated innovative systems with regard to renewable energy, sustainability and environmental and economic impact.
Ability to identify, formulate and solve industrial engineering problems, particularly in the energy field.
Ability to design, analyze, plan and manage energy conversion systems, and their environmental impact, as well as service and process plants, including complex and/or innovative ones.

Deep knowledge of the theoretical and scientific foundations of engineering, both in general and specifically in the areas of energy and electrical engineering, enabling the identification, formulation and solution of complex problems or problems requiring an interdisciplinary approach.

Deep knowledge of the theoretical and scientific foundations of mathematics and other basic sciences to interpret and describe complex engineering problems or those requiring an interdisciplinary approach.
Knowledge and use of scientific tools (software and other instruments) specific to the design sector within the field of energy engineering.
Knowledge of methods to conceive, plan, design and manage complex and/or innovative systems, processes and services.
Knowledge of advanced design tools (mechanical, thermo-fluid-dynamic, electrical or multi-physics) for the modeling and numerical simulation of components or systems.
Multidisciplinary knowledge of regulations, methods, technologies and tools relevant to the energy transition of systems, services and products.
Knowledge of the main renewable energy sources and energy storage systems and of the criteria for their integration with conventional production systems.

Principles and issues of heat exchange in machines and plants: systems and components of energy conversion machines and plants; modeling and computational simulation techniques; methodologies for optimized design, management and control of heat exchange networks.
Knowledge of the thermodynamic, thermo-fluid-dynamic, thermo-chemical and electrical phenomena underlying the main energy conversion systems.

Advanced topics in applied thermodynamics, thermoeconomics and environmental sustainability of plants, machines, components and systems for energy production and conversion; methodologies to identify thermodynamic and economic inefficiencies of energy systems and components; environmental and economic sustainability.
Ability to independently analyze data and information, draw objective conclusions and make consequential decisions.
Ability to evaluate different options or solutions to a problem and to make informed decisions about projects, including on the basis of relevant technical standards.
Ability to work in a coordinated group, with a clear understanding of the engineering problems context and the interdisciplinary implications of the application area.

Autonomy in meeting commitments and deadlines, including the ability to allocate time and available resources to meet deadlines, to accurately assess capabilities and resources to ensure commitments are realistic and achievable, and to prioritize activities based on importance and timing.
Ability to identify the need for new knowledge.
Ability to communicate and transfer information, ideas, problems and solutions to specialist and non-specialist audiences.
Ability to present professionally problems, solutions, analyses and results through written reports and oral presentations.
Skills in graphical representation and communication (preparation of diagrams, charts and tables).
Sustainability and ethical responsibility in engineering practice, including knowledge of environmental regulations and the ecological impact of engineering decisions.
Ability for autonomous and continuous learning and professional updating in the relevant engineering field.
Conducting bibliographic research using major resources (libraries, scientific databases, etc.).
Project- and problem-based learning: ability to learn through teaching methods based on projects and on solving real problems.
A successful student should have developed a good ability to choose transformers, generators and motors for industrial application and the student will understand operation principles and management.

syllabus_topics: Analysis of two-phase and three-phase circuits
Power of two-phase and three-phase circuits
Transformer in "alpha, beta" stationary reference frame and d,q rotating reference frame: Two-winding transformer
Synchronous machine in ", beta" stationary reference frame and d,q rotating reference frame: Cylindrical-rotor synchronous machine
Vector equation of cylindrical-rotor synchronous machine
Vector and phasor diagram of cylindrical-rotor synchronous generator
Asynchronous machine in ", beta" stationary reference frame and d,q rotating reference frame: Wound rotors and squirrel cage rotors
Vector equations of asynchronous machine, slip frequency
Direct-current machine: Armature windings, field excitation, armature reaction
Separately excited machine, shunt machine, series machine, compound machine
Motor starting and braking, speed control
Experimental tests of the transformer: parameters determination and operation of transformer without load, at full-load and in short-circuit
teaching_methods: Lectures supported by projector and PC

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam based on theoretical questions

assessment_rules: The oral exam assesses knowledge of operating principles, electromagnetic and mechanical behaviors of electrical machines, testing methods, ability to derive mathematical models, define equivalent circuit parameters and operating conditions, and select machines for applications. Grading ranges from Fail (Insufficient) for serious conceptual errors to 29-30 and Honors (Lode) for complete, in-depth, and well-structured knowledge, critical thinking, originality, and rigor. Honors are awarded for brilliance and originality exceeding standard expectations.
bibliography: A.E. Fitzgerald, C. Kingsley, and A. Kusko, " Electric Machinery" New York: McGraw-Hill Book Company, 1971.
L.W. Matsch and J.D. Morgan: Electromagnetic and Electromechanical Machines, New York: John Wiley & Sons, 1987.
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Meccanica (Mechanical Engineering), classe L-9 Classe delle lauree in Ingegneria industriale
